english_meaning: The large-scale clearing of forests, permanently destroying them for other land use.
gujarati_meaning: જંગલો કાપી-નાખ — મોટા પ્રમાણ પર — ખેતી, ઉ-ઉ (industry) અ-ઉ (or) ઉ-ઉ (construction) ઉ-ઉ (for).
usage_note: Deforestation releases carbon dioxide and destroys habitat; major driver of climate change.
memory_tip: 'De-' = ઘટ-ઉ (remove) + 'forest' = જ-ઉ (jungle) → remove forest = deforestation.
examples: Deforestation in the Amazon threatens thousands of species.
India loses millions of hectares to deforestation each year.
Deforestation contributes to soil erosion and flooding.
NGOs are working to reverse deforestation in tribal areas.

english_meaning: The total amount of greenhouse gases, especially carbon dioxide, produced by a person or activity.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (person/activity) ઉ-ઉ (total) CO₂ ઉ-ઉ (release) — carbon footprint.
usage_note: Reducing your carbon footprint involves eating less meat, flying less, using renewable energy.
memory_tip: 'Footprint' = ઉ-ઉ (mark you leave) → carbon footprint = ઉ-ઉ (CO₂) mark you leave.
examples: Flying has a very high carbon footprint.
Companies are measuring and reducing their carbon footprint.
Switching to electric vehicles lowers your carbon footprint.
Schools teach students how to calculate their carbon footprint.

english_meaning: The warming of the Earth caused by gases in the atmosphere trapping heat from the sun.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (atmosphere) ઉ-ઉ (gases) ઉ-ઉ (trap heat) — ઉ-ઉ (Earth) ઉ-ઉ (warms up).
usage_note: The greenhouse effect is natural and necessary; the enhanced version due to human activities causes global warming.
memory_tip: ઉ-ઉ (glass greenhouse traps warmth) → Earth's atmosphere does the same = greenhouse effect.
examples: The greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life.
Human activities are enhancing the greenhouse effect.
CO₂, methane, and water vapour are key greenhouse gases.
Understanding the greenhouse effect is essential for climate science.

english_meaning: The thinning of the ozone layer in the atmosphere, increasing UV radiation reaching Earth.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ozone layer) ઉ-ઉ (thin) ઉ-ઉ (UV rays) ઉ-ઉ (Earth reach) = ozone depletion.
usage_note: CFCs from aerosols were the main cause; the Montreal Protocol helped recovery.
memory_tip: 'Deplete' = ઘ-ઉ (decrease) → ozone depletes = ozone ઘ-ઉ (decreases).
examples: Ozone depletion over Antarctica led to the 'ozone hole'.
CFC gases were banned to slow ozone depletion.
Ozone depletion increases the risk of skin cancer.
The ozone layer is slowly recovering thanks to global action.

english_meaning: The introduction of harmful substances into the environment, damaging it.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (environment) ઉ-ઉ (harmful substances) ઉ-ઉ (intro) — ઉ-ઉ (damage).
usage_note: There are many types: air, water, soil, noise, and light pollution.
memory_tip: 'Pollute' = ઉ-ઉ (dirty) + '-ion' = process → pollution = ઉ-ઉ (making dirty).
examples: Air pollution in Delhi reaches dangerous levels in winter.
Industrial pollution has contaminated the river.
Noise pollution affects mental health in cities.
Strict laws are needed to curb plastic pollution.

english_meaning: Rain made acidic by atmospheric pollution, harming vegetation and water bodies.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (pollutants) ઉ-ઉ (rain + mix) → ઉ-ઉ (acidic rain) ઉ-ઉ (harms plants/water).
usage_note: Caused by SO₂ and NOₓ from burning fossil fuels; damages forests, lakes, and buildings.
memory_tip: 'Acid' = ઉ-ઉ (khatta/corrosive) + 'rain' = ઉ-ઉ (rain) → corrosive rain.
examples: Acid rain killed vast areas of forest in Europe in the 1980s.
Marble monuments are dissolving due to acid rain.
Power plants burning coal release gases that cause acid rain.
International agreements have reduced acid rain significantly.

english_meaning: Capable of being broken down naturally by bacteria or other living organisms.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (bacteria/organisms) ઉ-ઉ (naturally break down) — biodegradable.
usage_note: Biodegradable materials return to nature; non-biodegradable ones persist for centuries.
memory_tip: 'Bio' = life + 'degrade' = break down → breaks down by life = biodegradable.
examples: Paper and cotton are biodegradable materials.
Switching to biodegradable packaging reduces plastic waste.
Food waste is biodegradable and can be composted.
Not all 'eco-friendly' plastics are truly biodegradable.

english_meaning: The gradual wearing away of soil, rock, or land by wind, water, or other forces.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (wind/water) ઉ-ઉ (soil/rock) ઉ-ઉ (gradually wear away) — erosion.
usage_note: Deforestation accelerates erosion; roots hold soil in place.
memory_tip: 'Erode' = ઉ-ઉ (eat away) → erosion = ઉ-ઉ (eating away) of land.
examples: Coastal erosion is threatening cliffs and beaches.
Soil erosion reduces agricultural productivity.
Planting trees is an effective way to prevent erosion.
Erosion carved the spectacular landforms of Badlands National Park.

english_meaning: The ability to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (present needs) ઉ-ઉ (meet) ઉ-ઉ (future) ઉ-ઉ (compromise no) — sustainability.
usage_note: The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) address global sustainability challenges.
memory_tip: 'Sustain' = ટ-ઉ-ઉ (keep going) + '-ability' = ability → ability to keep going = sustainability.
examples: Sustainability is central to modern urban planning.
Solar energy is key to environmental sustainability.
Companies are adopting sustainability reporting practices.
The UN SDGs promote global sustainability by 2030.

english_meaning: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished, such as solar, wind, or hydro power.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (solar/wind/water) ઉ-ઉ (naturally refill) — renewable energy.
usage_note: India aims to achieve 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.
memory_tip: 'Renew' = ઉ-ઉ (refill/again) → renewable = ઉ-ઉ (energy that refills).
examples: Solar panels are the fastest-growing source of renewable energy.
India is a world leader in renewable energy expansion.
Renewable energy reduces dependence on imported oil.
Wind farms generate renewable energy without emissions.

english_meaning: Long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns, largely driven by human activities.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (global) ઉ-ઉ (temperature/weather) ઉ-ઉ (long-term change) — mostly human-caused.
usage_note: The IPCC reports that limiting warming to 1.5°C requires urgent global action.
memory_tip: 'Climate' = ઉ-ઉ (long-term weather) + 'change' = ઉ-ઉ (shift) → climate change.
examples: Climate change is causing more frequent extreme weather events.
The Paris Agreement aims to limit climate change to 1.5°C.
Small island nations face existential threats from climate change.
Young activists are demanding action on climate change.

english_meaning: The destruction or degradation of a natural environment that plants and animals depend on.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (animals/plants) ઉ-ઉ (home/environment) ઉ-ઉ (destroy/degrade) — habitat loss.
usage_note: Habitat loss is the primary driver of species extinction worldwide.
memory_tip: 'Habitat' = ઉ-ઉ (home) + 'loss' = ઉ-ઉ (destroy) → losing home = habitat loss.
examples: Habitat loss is the biggest threat to tigers in India.
Urban expansion causes widespread habitat loss.
Conservation corridors help mitigate habitat loss effects.
Habitat loss and poaching have pushed rhinos to near extinction.

english_meaning: A condition where the number of people or animals in an area exceeds what resources can sustainably support.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (people/animals) ઉ-ઉ (too many) — ઉ-ઉ (resources) ઉ-ઉ (not enough) — overpopulation.
usage_note: Overpopulation strains resources, increases pollution, and drives habitat loss.
memory_tip: 'Over' = ઉ-ઉ (too much) + 'population' = ઉ-ઉ (people) → too many people.
examples: Overpopulation in cities leads to housing and water shortages.
Wildlife overpopulation can strip an area of vegetation.
Deer overpopulation in suburbs causes crop and garden damage.
Sustainable development addresses challenges posed by overpopulation.

english_meaning: The process by which fertile land becomes desert, often due to drought and overuse.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (fertile land) ઉ-ઉ (desert) ઉ-ઉ (become) — usually drought + overuse caused.
usage_note: The Sahel region of Africa faces severe desertification; the Great Green Wall project combats it.
memory_tip: 'Desert' + '-ification' = process of becoming desert = desertification.
examples: Overgrazing is accelerating desertification in arid regions.
Desertification threatens food security for millions.
The Great Green Wall aims to stop desertification across Africa.
Planting drought-resistant trees can reverse desertification.

english_meaning: The long-term storage of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to reduce greenhouse gases.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (CO₂) ઉ-ઉ (long-term store) — forests/soil/ocean ઉ-ઉ (trap) CO₂.
usage_note: Forests are the most effective natural carbon sinks; oceans absorb about 30% of CO₂.
memory_tip: 'Sequester' = ઉ-ઉ (hold apart/store) → carbon sequestration = store carbon away.
examples: Forests are vital for carbon sequestration.
Peatlands store more carbon than all the world's forests combined.
Carbon sequestration technology is being developed for power plants.
Protecting wetlands enhances natural carbon sequestration.

english_meaning: The deterioration of the natural environment through depletion of resources and destruction of ecosystems.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (natural environment) ઉ-ઉ (resources deplete) ઉ-ઉ (ecosystems destroy) — deterioration.
usage_note: Addressing environmental degradation requires both policy and individual action.
memory_tip: 'Degrade' = ઉ-ઉ (reduce quality) → environmental degradation = reducing environment's quality.
examples: Rapid industrialisation has caused severe environmental degradation.
Environmental degradation reduces the quality of life in rural areas.
The UN calls environmental degradation a global emergency.
Community-based conservation can reverse environmental degradation.

english_meaning: A sudden violent shaking of the ground caused by movements of the Earth's tectonic plates.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (tectonic plates) ઉ-ઉ (move) → ઉ-ઉ (ground) ઉ-ઉ (shake violently) — earthquake.
usage_note: Measured on the Richter scale or moment magnitude scale; above 7.0 is very strong.
memory_tip: 'Earth' + 'quake' = ઉ-ઉ (Earth) + ઉ-ઉ (shaking) = earthquake.
examples: The 2001 Bhuj earthquake devastated Gujarat.
Earthquake-resistant buildings are essential in seismic zones.
A 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck Turkey in 2023.
Early warning systems can save lives during earthquakes.

english_meaning: A series of giant ocean waves caused by an underwater earthquake, landslide, or volcanic eruption.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (underwater earthquake/eruption) ઉ-ઉ (giant waves) ઉ-ઉ (coast) ઉ-ઉ (hit) — tsunami.
usage_note: The 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami killed over 200,000 people across 14 countries.
memory_tip: Japanese word: 'tsu' = harbour + 'nami' = wave → harbour wave = tsunami.
examples: The 2004 tsunami devastated coastal areas across Southeast Asia.
A tsunami warning system was established after 2004.
Tsunamis can travel at 800 km/h across open ocean.
Coastal communities practise tsunami evacuation drills.

english_meaning: A large, destructive system of winds rotating around a centre of low pressure over the ocean.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ocean) ઉ-ઉ (low pressure centre) ઉ-ઉ (rotating winds) — ઉ-ઉ (destructive).
usage_note: Called hurricane in Atlantic, typhoon in Pacific, cyclone in Indian Ocean.
memory_tip: 'Cyclo-' = circle → cyclone = ઉ-ઉ (circular) rotating storm.
examples: Cyclone Biparjoy hit Gujarat's coast in June 2023.
A severe cyclone warning was issued for Odisha's coast.
Cyclones draw energy from warm ocean water.
Thousands were evacuated before the cyclone made landfall.

english_meaning: The sudden release of magma, gases, and ash from a volcano onto the Earth's surface.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (volcano) ઉ-ઉ (lava/ash/gases) ઉ-ઉ (suddenly release) — volcanic eruption.
usage_note: Can affect global climate by releasing ash and sulphur dioxide into the atmosphere.
memory_tip: 'Erupt' = ઉ-ઉ (burst out) → volcanic eruption = ઉ-ઉ (lava burst).
examples: The 1980 Mount St Helens eruption caused massive destruction.
Volcanic eruptions can disrupt air travel with ash clouds.
Indonesia sits on the Ring of Fire and has frequent eruptions.
Lava from the eruption reached the sea within hours.

english_meaning: The rapid movement of a mass of earth, rock, or debris down a hillside.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (hill) ઉ-ઉ (soil/rock/debris) ઉ-ઉ (rapidly slide down) — landslide.
usage_note: Common during monsoons in hilly regions; deforestation increases landslide risk.
memory_tip: 'Land' + 'slide' = ઉ-ઉ (land) + ઉ-ઉ (slide) = land slides down.
examples: A landslide buried the mountain village during heavy rain.
Deforestation increases the risk of landslides.
The Wayanad landslide of 2024 was one of India's deadliest.
Early warning systems can reduce landslide casualties.

english_meaning: A sudden, violent flood caused by extremely heavy rainfall in a short time.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (sudden heavy rain) → ઉ-ઉ (rapid flooding) — flash flood.
usage_note: Flash floods can occur with little warning; particularly dangerous in valleys and urban areas.
memory_tip: 'Flash' = ઉ-ઉ (sudden, like flash of light) + 'flood' = ઉ-ઉ (flood) → sudden flood.
examples: A flash flood swept through the desert canyon without warning.
Flash floods in Himachal Pradesh killed dozens in 2023.
Urban areas are increasingly prone to flash floods.
People should never try to drive through a flash flood.

english_meaning: An uncontrolled fire that spreads rapidly through vegetation in rural or wilderness areas.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (uncontrolled fire) ઉ-ઉ (forest/rural) ઉ-ઉ (rapid spread) — wildfire.
usage_note: Climate change is making wildfires more frequent and severe.
memory_tip: 'Wild' = ઉ-ઉ (uncontrolled, in the wild) + 'fire' = ઉ-ઉ (fire) → wildfire.
examples: Wildfires burned millions of hectares in Australia in 2019-2020.
Climate change is making wildfire seasons longer and more intense.
Firefighters battled the wildfire for weeks before containing it.
Wildfires release huge amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

english_meaning: An abnormal rise of water level along a coast due to storm winds pushing sea water ashore.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (storm) ઉ-ઉ (winds) ઉ-ઉ (push seawater) ઉ-ઉ (coast) — storm surge.
usage_note: Storm surges are the deadliest aspect of hurricanes and cyclones for coastal communities.
memory_tip: 'Surge' = ઉ-ઉ (sudden rise) + storm → storm surge = sudden sea rise during storm.
examples: The storm surge during Cyclone Amphan flooded Kolkata's streets.
Storm surges are more dangerous than the wind itself.
Coastal embankments protect against storm surges.
Low-lying island nations are most vulnerable to storm surges.

english_meaning: A large mass of snow and ice that suddenly falls down a mountain.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (mountain) ઉ-ઉ (snow/ice mass) ઉ-ઉ (suddenly fall) — avalanche.
usage_note: Avalanches can be triggered by heavy snowfall, vibrations, or warming temperatures.
memory_tip: 'Aval-' → 'avval' (first/fast) → fast-falling snow = avalanche.
examples: An avalanche buried the ski resort in metres of snow.
Mountaineers carry avalanche beacons for safety.
Loud sounds can trigger an avalanche on unstable slopes.
Avalanche warnings were issued across the Himalayan region.

english_meaning: A critical state of water shortage declared when drought causes severe humanitarian or economic crisis.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (water shortage) ઉ-ઉ (severe crisis) ઉ-ઉ (declared emergency) — drought emergency.
usage_note: Governments declare drought emergencies to mobilize resources for affected regions.
memory_tip: 'Drought' = ઉ-ઉ (no water) + 'emergency' = ઉ-ઉ (crisis) → water crisis.
examples: The state declared a drought emergency after three failed monsoons.
Drought emergencies trigger food and water relief programmes.
Climate change is increasing the frequency of drought emergencies.
Farmers demand compensation during declared drought emergencies.

english_meaning: The frequency, type, and size of earthquakes and ground movement in a region over a period of time.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (earthquakes/ground movement) ઉ-ઉ (frequency/type/size) — seismic activity.
usage_note: Seismographs record seismic activity; seismologists study earthquake patterns.
memory_tip: 'Seismic' = ભૂ-ઉ-ઉ (earth-shake) → seismic activity = earth-shake events.
examples: Seismic activity in the Himalayan region is closely monitored.
Increased seismic activity preceded the volcanic eruption.
Scientists use GPS to track seismic activity and plate movement.
Gujarat lies in a high seismic activity zone.

english_meaning: A smaller earthquake that follows the main earthquake in the same area.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (main earthquake) ઉ-ઉ (after) ઉ-ઉ (same area) ઉ-ઉ (smaller quake) — aftershock.
usage_note: Aftershocks can be nearly as strong as the main quake and cause additional damage.
memory_tip: 'After' + 'shock' = ઉ-ઉ (after) + ઉ-ઉ (shock) → shock that comes after.
examples: Dozens of aftershocks followed the main earthquake.
Rescue workers are always alert to aftershocks during operations.
A powerful aftershock collapsed already weakened buildings.
Aftershocks can continue for weeks after a major earthquake.

english_meaning: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (earthquake origin) ઉ-ઉ (directly above surface point) — epicentre.
usage_note: The epicentre experiences the strongest shaking; damage decreases with distance.
memory_tip: 'Epi-' = above + 'centre' = ઉ-ઉ (centre) → the centre point above the quake origin.
examples: The epicentre of the earthquake was 20 km north of the city.
Buildings near the epicentre were completely flattened.
Scientists located the epicentre using seismograph data.
The epicentre of the 2001 Bhuj quake was in Kutch district.

english_meaning: An official alert issued by meteorological authorities warning of an approaching dangerous storm.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (meteorological) ઉ-ઉ (official alert) ઉ-ઉ (dangerous storm approaching) — storm warning.
usage_note: Storm warnings are issued in colour codes (yellow, orange, red) based on severity.
memory_tip: 'Storm' + 'warning' = ઉ-ઉ (danger storm) + ઉ-ઉ (alert) → storm warning.
examples: A storm warning was issued for the entire coastal district.
Residents were advised to stay indoors during the red storm warning.
The storm warning allowed thousands to evacuate in time.
Weather agencies improve storm warnings using satellite data.

english_meaning: The flooding and submersion of a flat area beside a river during high water levels.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (river) ઉ-ઉ (high water) → ઉ-ઉ (floodplain) ઉ-ઉ (submerge) — inundation.
usage_note: Regular inundation deposits fertile silt; but excessive flooding devastates communities.
memory_tip: 'Inundate' = ઉ-ઉ (flood over) → inundation = submersion in water.
examples: The annual inundation of the Nile enriched Egypt's farmlands.
Flood plain inundation in Bihar affects millions of farmers.
Inundation maps help identify areas at risk of flooding.
The floodplain was inundated for weeks after the dam overflow.

english_meaning: A storm in which hail (balls of ice) falls, sometimes causing severe damage to crops and property.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (ice balls) ઉ-ઉ (fall in storm) — ઉ-ઉ (crops/property damage) — hailstorm.
usage_note: Hailstones can be as large as golf balls or bigger; cause millions in crop damage annually.
memory_tip: 'Hail' = ઉ-ઉ (ice pellets) + 'storm' = ઉ-ઉ (storm) → ice-pellet storm.
examples: A hailstorm destroyed most of the wheat crop in minutes.
Large hailstones shattered car windscreens across the city.
Farmers lost their entire harvest to a sudden hailstorm.
Hailstorm warnings are issued by meteorological departments in spring.
